questions.q: All the following are typical characteristics of a **dependent branch** EXCEPT that
options: Goods for resale are supplied to the branch exclusively by the Head Office
It maintains a complete and independent set of double-entry ledger books locally
All cash collections from sales are banked promptly into the Head Office account
Small day-to-day branch operating expenses are reimbursed via an imprest petty cash system
questions.explain: A **dependent branch** does not maintain a complete set of accounting records; all its main accounting entries and ledger accounts are kept centrally by the **Head Office**. An *independent branch*, on the other hand, keeps full double-entry books and extracts its own trial balance.

questions.q: In the Head Office books under the Debtors System for a dependent branch, what is the double entry for recording **goods sent to the branch at cost price**?
options: Debit Branch Account; Credit Goods Sent to Branch Account
Debit Goods Sent to Branch Account; Credit Branch Account
Debit Purchases Account; Credit Branch Debtors Account
Debit Branch Account; Credit Sales Account
questions.explain:
Under the Debtors System in the Head Office ledger:
*   **Debit Branch Account** (to record the value of assets/inventory entrusted to the branch).
*   **Credit Goods Sent to Branch Account** (which at the end of the year is transferred to the credit of the Trading/Purchases Account to reduce total purchases).

questions.q: A Head Office invoices goods to its branch at cost plus a mark-up of $25\%$. During the period, goods with an invoice price of ₦100,000 were sent to the branch. What is the value of the **loading (unrealized profit)** to be credited to the Branch Stock Adjustment Account?
questions.explain:
1.  **Mark-up on Cost:** $25\% = \frac{1}{4}$ on cost.
2.  **Equivalent Margin on Invoice Price:** $\frac{1}{4+1} = \frac{1}{5} = 20\%$ on invoice price.
3.  **Calculation of Loading:**
    $$\text{Loading} = 20\% \times ₦100,000 = ₦20,000$$

*(Alternatively, if $\text{Cost} = 100\%$ and $\text{Invoice} = 125\%$, then $\text{Cost} = \frac{₦100,000}{1.25} = ₦80,000$. The loading is $₦100,000 - ₦80,000 = ₦20,000$).*
